s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with fever, quadriplegia, and brainstem involvement
salient_findings: Bilateral horizontal gaze palsy with impaired oculocephalic reflexes
Quadriplegia with bilateral extensor plantar responses
T1 hypointensity and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the bilateral thalami, pons, medulla, and left cerebellum on MRI
key_facts: 1 day of weakness in all four limbs and speech difficulty
Anemia, reduced packed cell volume, and thrombocytopenia on laboratory evaluation
Normal total cell count (all lymphocytes) and mildly elevated protein on cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Serum dengue NS1 antigen was positive
MRI showed intense diffusion restriction on DWI and central blooming on GRE sequences

shortlist.label: Dengue encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Serum dengue NS1 antigen was positive and patient has acute neurological syndrome with fever and brainstem involvement

shortlist.label: Japanese encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has acute neurological syndrome with fever, quadriplegia, and brainstem involvement, which are common features of Japanese encephalitis

shortlist.label: Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has brainstem involvement, bilateral horizontal gaze palsy, and impaired oculocephalic reflexes, which are characteristic of Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis

shortlist.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has acute neurological syndrome with fever, quadriplegia, and brainstem involvement, and MRI shows intense diffusion restriction on DWI and central blooming on GRE sequences

shortlist.label: West Nile virus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has acute neurological syndrome with fever, quadriplegia, and brainstem involvement, which are common features of West Nile virus encephalitis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, vomiting, and neurological deficits, combined with the presence of serum dengue NS1 antigen and the characteristic MRI findings, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Japanese encephalitis
rejected.why: No specific evidence of Japanese encephalitis virus infection was provided

rejected.label: Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis
rejected.why: Lack of typical Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis symptoms such as ophthalmoplegia and ataxia

rejected.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: The presence of serum dengue NS1 antigen and the specific MRI findings are more consistent with dengue encephalitis

rejected.label: West Nile virus encephalitis
rejected.why: No evidence of West Nile virus infection was provided, and the clinical presentation and MRI findings are more consistent with dengue encephalitis
